cves.headline: Langflow 1.5.0-1.10.3 lets users spoof localhost and overwrite MCP config

name: Authentication Bypass by Spoofing
title: CWE-290: Authentication Bypass by Spoofing
ai_text: In AI software this weakness shows up in agent frameworks and MCP servers, where trust is often decided by where a request appears to come from. The one CVE here is in Langflow, a low code tool for building LLM applications and agents. Versions 1.5.0 through 1.10.3 accept a spoofed localhost origin, so a remote caller can look like a local one. That lets the attacker overwrite the MCP configuration, which controls which tools and servers the agent may reach. Once that config is changed, the attacker can point the agent at their own tooling. The result is access to agent behaviour and connected services without ever passing a real login.
description: This attack-focused weakness is caused by incorrectly implemented authentication schemes that are subject to spoofing attacks.

consequences.note: This weakness can allow an attacker to access resources which are not otherwise accessible without proper authentication.
